Definition: from the particle αὖ (perhaps akin to the base of G109 through the idea of a baffling wind) (backward); the reflexive pronoun self, used (alone or in the compound G1438) of the third person, and (with the proper personal pronoun) of the other persons:--her, it(-self), one, the other, (mine) own, said, (self-), the) same, ((him-, my-, thy-)self, (your-)selves, she, that, their(-s), them(-selves), there(-at, - by, -in, -into, -of, -on, -with), they, (these) things, this (man), those, together, very, which. Compare G848.
BiblicalUsage: This is the plain pronoun behind he, she, it, they, them and himself — thousands of times over, it is the word that points back to someone already named. In John 1:3 all things were made by him, in John 3:16 God gave his Son for the world, and in Romans 8:29 we are conformed to the image of his Son. The word itself carries no meaning of its own; it borrows everything from the person it points to.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this little word quietly teaches me something large: Scripture is never vague about who did what. When it says he, it means a real person — Christ himself, God himself — and my faith rests on him, not on an idea.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
